name: InMode Lumecca

lead: Lumecca is a light-based clinic treatment for skin tone. It is used on sun spots, uneven pigment and visible redness on the face, neck, chest and hands.
People use it for a clearer, more uniform complexion, usually in a few sessions spaced weeks apart.

paras: Intense pulsed light delivers broad-spectrum pulses that pigment and blood vessels absorb. The targeted spots darken and flake off, and redness fades as small vessels are treated.
Temporary redness, swelling and spot darkening are commonly described. Pigment changes and burns are less common, and providers usually discuss tanning, skin tone and sun protection beforehand.

angle.text: Lumecca is used to even out skin colour by targeting sun spots, freckle-like pigment and facial redness. People book it for a clearer, more uniform complexion, often across a few sessions.

lead: InMode Lumecca is an intense pulsed light (IPL) device from the aesthetics company InMode, used in clinics to improve skin tone and clarity. It is mainly offered for brown spots, sun damage, and visible redness or small surface vessels on the face, neck, chest and hands.

People use it to get a more even, clearer complexion: pigment and redness are targeted with broad-spectrum light pulses, and treated spots typically darken and flake away over the following days. Clinics commonly schedule a short series of sessions.

IPL works through a xenon flashlamp that emits broad-spectrum light; filters remove unwanted wavelengths, and the light is absorbed by melanin and haemoglobin, which are heated and broken down. [1] The technology was invented by Shimon Eckhouse in 1992, and the FDA approved it for vascular lesions in 1995 and pigmented lesions in 1996. [1] InMode's earlier SR IPL device was cleared by the FDA in 2013 for benign pigmented epidermal lesions and cutaneous vascular lesions, with a 515 to 1200 nm output. [2]

A registered clinical trial (2025) studied IPL, an anti-redness dermocosmetic and their combination for rosacea, which places IPL-type treatment within research on facial redness. [3] No published study names Lumecca itself.

paras: Lumecca is a provider-operated IPL platform. IPL devices emit a range of light wavelengths that are absorbed by pigment (melanin) and by haemoglobin in blood vessels, which is why they are used for both brown spots and redness. Unlike lasers, which use a single wavelength, IPL uses interchangeable filters to target different chromophores. [1]

The InMode SR IPL, cleared in 2013, lists fluence of 10 to 30 J/cm2, a 10 by 30 mm spot and contact cooling. Its indications cover dyschromia, hyperpigmentation, melasma and freckles, as well as port wine stains, telangiectasias, rosacea, angiomas and superficial leg veins. [2]

Wikipedia lists IPL uses including sun damage, freckles, liver spots and melasma, where repeated sessions can clear dyschromia, and vascular lesions such as thread veins and rosacea, where it is described as at least as effective as pulsed dye lasers. [1] Appearance-focused users seek IPL to even out skin tone and reduce visible redness without peeling or surgery. Providers commonly advise sun protection before and after treatment.

IPL is generally considered safe, though complications such as hyperpigmentation can occur; photosensitising medications and existing skin damage are contraindications, and a manufacturer states it is best suited to light-to-medium skin tones. [1] Commonly reported effects include temporary redness, swelling and darkening of treated spots before they fade; recent tanning or darker skin tones are usually discussed with the provider beforehand.

A 2025 registered trial (NCT07729540, 60 participants, listed as completed) compared IPL, an anti-redness dermocosmetic and the two combined in the treatment of rosacea. [3] It does not name a specific device, and no published results for Lumecca itself are listed. The FDA summary for the earlier InMode SR IPL states that clinical performance data were not applicable, since it was cleared on equivalence to existing devices. [2]
